[ASSISTANT_SAID] Swimming is an excellent way to improve cardiovascular endurance while being easy on the joints.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended warm-up: Easy swimming with a mix of freestyle, backstroke, and breaststroke; dynamic stretching, such as arm circles and leg kicks.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Endurance Sets: Swim 4-6 sets of 200-400 meters at a moderate pace (60-70% effort); rest for 20-30 seconds between sets.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Interval Training: Swim 25-50 meters at a high intensity (80-90% effort); rest for 15-25 seconds; repeat for 8-12 reps; cool down with easy swimming for 25-50 meters.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Pyramid Workout: Swim 25 meters at a moderate pace; increase distance by 25 meters each set; decrease distance by 25 meters after reaching the peak; rest for 20-30 seconds between sets.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Sprint Intervals with Kicking: Swim 25 meters at a high intensity (80-90% effort) with a kickboard; rest for 15-25 seconds; repeat for 8-12 reps; cool down with easy swimming for 25-50 meters.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Long, Steady-State Swim: Swim at a moderate pace (60-70% effort) for 10-20 minutes; focus on maintaining a consistent pace and efficient technique.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended cool-down: Easy swimming with a mix of freestyle, backstroke, and breaststroke; static stretching, such as hamstring and shoulder stretches.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips to Improve Endurance: Incorporate strength training, drills, mix up strokes, gradually increase distance and intensity, and make it fun.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested focusing on technique, building endurance, incorporating drills, strength training, practicing open-water swimming, and swim-specific workouts for triathlon training.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Sample swim workout includes warm-up, drills, endurance set, sprint intervals, and cool-down.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested tracking progress by logging workouts, using a training plan
